goal: Teach Year-2 physics students to turn a familiar two-loop DC circuit into two Kirchhoff equations, map the equations into a 2x2 system, solve with MATLAB backslash, reconstruct the shared-branch current, validate the original equations directly, and interpret the signs physically.

deck_context.deck_context: Week 03 uses one small two-loop resistor circuit so the new cognitive load is representation: choose mesh-current directions, write one Kirchhoff voltage equation per loop, map each equation to one matrix row, solve the supplied system, and return to the circuit for validation and interpretation.
deck_context.core_claim: A matrix is a compact representation of physical equations; a solver result becomes credible only when the original equations are checked and the currents are interpreted using the stated directions and units.
deck_context.locked_model: Two clockwise mesh currents I1 and I2; R1 = 2 ohm; R2 = 3 ohm; Rs = 1 ohm; V1 = 5 V; V2 = 2 V; Ishared = I1 - I2; (R1+Rs)I1 - Rs I2 = V1; -Rs I1 + (R2+Rs)I2 = V2; A_ohm = [3 -1; -1 4]; b_V = [5; 2]; x_A = A_ohm\b_V; I1_A = 2 A; I2_A = 1 A; Ishared_A = 1 A.
deck_context.exactness: Equations, matrix entries, code, variable names, values, units, signs, assertion tolerance, and validation differences are strict teaching content. Do not invent, paraphrase, or approximate them.

core: map one equation to one matrix row
interpret positive and negative current signs

slides.intent: Open with the physical question and establish that A*x=b stores circuit equations rather than replacing the physics.
key_points: A two-loop circuit can be written as two equations.
A 2x2 system stores those equations compactly.
MATLAB can solve the system.
The result still needs a physical check.

slides.title: Audit the matrix before asking MATLAB to solve
slides.intent: Prevent sign and row/column mistakes by reading every coefficient back as physics.
key_points: A11 = R1 + Rs = 3 ohm.
A12 = -Rs = -1 ohm.
A21 = -Rs = -1 ohm.
A22 = R2 + Rs = 4 ohm.

slides.title: A plausible matrix can still encode the wrong circuit
slides.intent: Distinguish successful MATLAB execution from a physically correct model.

The correct equations expose a -1.6923 V mismatch in the left equation.
Successful execution is not proof of a correct model.
